overview: Dengue is a viral infection caused by the dengue virus, transmitted to humans through the bite of infected mosquitoes, mostly in tropical and sub-tropical climates. Most people who get dengue do not have symptoms, but for those who do, the most common symptoms are high fever, headache, body aches, nausea and rash. In severe cases, dengue can be fatal.
treatment: pain management with medication such as paracetamol (acetaminophen)
hospitalization for people with severe dengue
transmission: infected female mosquitoes, primarily the Aedes aegypti mosquito
risk_factors: living in tropical and sub-tropical climates
being infected for the second time
key_facts: about half of the world's population is now at risk of dengue
an estimated 100–400 million infections occur each year
5.6 billion people are at risk of infection with dengue and other arboviruses
